memoryText: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we have seen his glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read John 1:14 slowly, several times, and say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This single verse is the heart of the Christmas message, and of the whole Gospel of John.

“The Word.” In Greek, logos. To Greek readers, it was the rational order behind the universe. To Jewish readers, it was God’s creative and revealing speech. John says that this Word is a person, the eternal Son who was with God and was God.

“Became flesh.” Flesh means our weak, mortal humanity. He did not hover above it. He took it on. The infinite entered the finite, and the Creator became a creature.

“And dwelt among us.” The verb is “tabernacled.” Just as God’s glory filled the tent in the wilderness, so God’s glory now lives in a human body. God has pitched his tent in our neighborhood.

“We have seen his glory.” John is a witness. He saw the glory on the mountain, at Cana, and at the cross. It was a glory of weakness as well as power.

“Full of grace and truth.” Grace is God’s free favor. Truth is God’s faithfulness and reality. In Christ we get both.

When you wonder what God is like, say this verse. Look at Jesus.
weekInReview: This week you finished the Gospel of Luke, with the cross, the thief’s prayer, the empty tomb, and the walk to Emmaus, where Jesus opened the Scriptures and showed that they are about him. Then you began the Gospel of John. The prologue told you that the Word who was with God and was God became flesh and dwelt among us. Your doctrinal pause on the incarnation set John’s words beside Philippians 2 and Colossians 1: the one who made all things emptied himself, became a servant, and died on a cross. In John 2 and 3 you saw Jesus turn water into wine, cleanse the temple, and tell Nicodemus that he must be born again. You met the verse that sums up the Gospel: “For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son.”
reflectionQuestions: John says the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. What does it mean for you that God chose to live among us as a human being?
Jesus’ first sign was turning water into wine, a picture of the joy of the new covenant. How does Jesus bring joy where there was only emptiness?
Nicodemus came by night with questions. What is one honest question you would bring to Jesus right now?
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for dwelling among us, full of grace and truth.
